the policy prompt for subgoal
  Failures occurred when selecting among free cubes for one red, four red, three blue plus one green, and one red plus two blue. The policy correctly initialized or updated the deposit counters, and correctly continued picking when quotas remained, but selected the wrong same-color cube using the smallest-y fallback or an insufficiently matching existing layout preference. These are SUFFICIENCY failures in target selection, not counter PREDICTABILITY failures. Keep the existing memory fields, deposit recognition, quota checks, A/B/C transitions, and existing layout preferences. Add the following complete goal-and-layout preferences before the fallback, using updated counters and matching reference locations to currently observed objects. For a one-red goal with the bin near [99, 172], select the red cube near [69, 179]. Distinguishing red arrangement landmarks are [60, 148], [79, 153], [100, 97], [113, 132], and [116, 86]. This arrangement must not inherit the existing one-red preference selecting near [98, 84]; a nearby bin or a single nearby red cube is not enough to match that other preference. For a four-red goal with the bin near [136, 82], select red near [71, 141], [91, 162], [62, 132], or [57, 160] when updated red_deposited is respectively zero, one, two, or three. The initial scene may show only the first red candidate. Later-visible landmarks include blue near [55, 126], [81, 95], and [95, 115], and red near [67, 167], [105, 181], and [108, 152]. After the first deposit, the smaller-y reds do not override the indexed target near [91, 162]; after the second deposit, select near [62, 132], not near [57, 160]. For three blue and one green with the bin near [116, 107], finish green first, selecting green near [65, 109] while green_deposited is zero. After that green deposit, select blue near [85, 111], [105, 188], or [92, 96] when updated blue_deposited is respectively zero, one, or two. Additional landmarks, when visible, are blue near [62, 85] and [81, 78], green near [53, 130] and [118, 180], and red near [70, 125], [89, 134], [94, 165], and [95, 73]. The smaller-y blue landmarks are not preferred targets. Do not turn this preference into a universal green-first rule. For one red and two blue with the bin near [118, 108], finish red first, selecting red near [55, 144], not the other red near [52, 80]. After one red deposit, select blue near [90, 96] when updated blue_deposited is zero, then blue near [113, 168] when it is one. Additional landmarks are blue near [63, 77], [63, 157], [72, 163], and [76, 148], and green near [85, 79], [88, 160], and [101, 81]. These smaller-y blue cubes do not override the indexed targets. Apply these preferences only when the requested quantities, bin, and observable remaining arrangement jointly match. Missing initial candidates that are later revealed, already deposited candidates, and temporary occlusions do not by themselves invalidate a match. Use current visible positions and output a point within the selected cube in [y, x] order, rather than treating reference coordinates as fixed action points. Preserve the existing fallback for unfamiliar layouts or unavailable preferred candidates, but do not apply it ahead of a matching preference. No existing rule needs deletion.
